title: Canonical signed addition for the actual finite coefficient lines
statement: For the finite-coefficient setting [def-pur-conventions] and its actual integral-reduced signed lines in fixed-scalar coordinates [def-pur-finite-tensor-reduction-data], define a coherent local frame to consist of one basis of every signed line: the zero basis is 1, the positive bases are the prescribed ordered powers of the first basis, and each negative basis evaluates to 1 on its positive dual basis. Define signed tensor addition by the unique sheaf isomorphisms taking each product of coherent frame basis vectors to the sum-degree basis vector. Their degree-zero derived versions are the unique isomorphisms whose arrows are the canonical single-complex tensor map followed by the single of the sheaf product. Use that map from [def-pur-supported-cup]; flatness of the lines makes it invertible, including opposite-sign cancellation and zero powers. Its derived normalization is the equation of [def-pur-finite-tensor-comparison-equations].

proof.text: For each pair of integer degrees use the normalized ordinary morphism existence theorem. Choose these morphisms in the proof only. Apply the local basis-isomorphism criterion to each one, and package each actual morphism with asIso. Their normalization is the existence theorem's equation.

For any other normalized family, apply function extensionality in both degrees and Iso.ext. The frame detection lemma reduces equality of their homs to their realized values on a frame tensor. Both normalizations identify those values with the same sum-degree basis, proving equality.

For the derived product, first prove flatness of finiteTensorFixedSheaf. Transport coefficientTwistFiniteRank across Nat.sub_add_cancel for the prescribed first line; the coefficient prime is invertible in residue fields by coefficientPrime_isUnit_stalk and the residue map. coefficientTwistLine_exact gives finite-limit preservation of intrinsic right tensor by every signed line. Identify the realization of the fixed sheaf with that line using the equivalence counit and siteSheafTensorRightIso. The intrinsic right-tensor comparison and reflection of finite limits by the equivalence give finite-limit preservation for fixed-scalar right tensor. Braiding and flat_iff_preservesFiniteLimits give flatness.

Apply the already proved private cupSingleTensorMap_isIso from SupportedCup to this flat first input. Compose its invertible canonical tensor-to-single arrow with the single-functor image of finiteTensorSheafProducts. Take asIso of that actual composite. The normalization holds by HEq.rfl; any other normalized isomorphism has the same hom by eq_of_heq, so Iso.ext proves uniqueness.
